t: A prince-electorate of the Holy Roman Empire on the Elbe, ruled from 1423 by the Wettin dynasty from Wittenberg and later Dresden.
Frederick the Wise protected Martin Luther, making Saxony the birthplace of the Lutheran Reformation.
Under Augustus the Strong, King of Poland from 1697, Dresden became a Baroque capital and Meissen made Europe’s first hard-paste porcelain.
dyk: Saxony’s Erzgebirge silver was struck from about 1500 into some of the first large silver coins of the type later called the thaler, the name that lives on in the word dollar.
ev: The Golden Bull confirms the Duke of Saxe-Wittenberg as a prince-elector
Emperor Sigismund grants the electorate to Frederick the Warlike of Meissen
The Division of Leipzig splits the Wettin lands between Ernest and Albert
Martin Luther publishes his theses at Wittenberg
Charles V wins at Mühlberg; the electorate passes to Maurice
Augustus the Strong is elected King of Poland
Frederick the Great invades; the Saxon army capitulates at Pirna
Frederick Augustus III becomes King of Saxony

f.founder: Rudolf I of Saxe-Wittenberg; Frederick the Warlike (Wettin)
